newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks put on mild gains after tight trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks put on mild gains after tight trade.

text.p: Greek shares settled a touch higher after tight range trading with industrials and banks ending firmer but small-caps and construction giving ground. Trading volume was light.

"The 901 level on the benchmark index has been repeatedly tested and proven to be a strong support level. Many stocks are underpriced offering good yields. At current price levels 1996 dividend yields will be more attractive than a year earlier," said Kappa Securities in its weekly outlook.

"The attractiveness is reinforced by the already sharp decline of one-year T-bill yields down to 11.5 percent which will be further reduced after the taxation of earned interest in 1997. This justifies our view that the market's upside potential will emerge very soon," it said.
Meanwhile farmers continued a 19-day blockade of major highways and road links protesting against Greece's austere 1997 budget.
They were demanding lower diesel fuel prices, cuts in the VAT tax on farm equipment, rescheduling of the debts by farm cooperatives to state banks and higher price supports especially for cotton.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis has refused to bow to farmers' demands as they threatened to stage a mass protest in Athens on Wednesday.

And teachers and seamen opened a week of strikes on Monday protesting against the government's tough 1997 budget. Greece's largest labour confederations representing civil servants, workers, doctors, bank employees will join in this week.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.20 percent or 1.82 points higher at 907.68 from Friday's 905.86 close after opening at 904.49. Turnover was 2.98 billion drachmas on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Decliners led gainers 104 to 69 with 31 issues unchanged on 204 traded. Banks rose 0.11 percent, industrials gained 0.71 percent but construction slippedg 0.09 percent. Small-caps lost 0.30 percent.
